title: Mass Measured, Energy Analyzed: A Constructive Note on the POWERS Analytical Framework
content: The Physiology Of the Weight Reduced State (POWERS) study is the most comprehensive empirical investigation of energy balance in weight-reduced humans ever designed. Its measurement battery – doubly labeled water, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, whole-room calorimetry, ventilated-hood indirect calorimetry, actigraphy, and multi-pass dietary recall – represents the state of the art. This commentary makes a single observation about one analytical choice. POWERS measures fat mass and fat-free mass directly with DXA in grams. It then converts these mass measurements to energy using fixed coefficients (9.3 and 1.1 kcal/g) and uses energy as the primary analytical variable. The conversion is not required by the data. The mass measurements are already in the units the body handles. The coefficients are literature values, not measurements within POWERS. The measurement chain is mass-based from the beginning: DLW measures CO₂ production, which is a mass flux. This commentary suggests that POWERS report both mass-based and energy-based analyses side by side. POWERS is in a rare position: it has the data – or will have the data – to test whether the two frameworks give the same conclusions. If they agree, the energy framework is validated. If they diverge, the divergence is itself informative. Either outcome would strengthen the paper. The suggestion is a refinement, not a correction.
